question: Should OpenClaw accept static SecretRef values in sandbox.docker.env when the resolved values still become Docker environment variables visible through Docker/container metadata?
rationale: The source gap is clear and the implementation path is bounded, but the permanent security/product boundary needs a human decision before the linked PR can close the issue.

options.title: Accept with explicit boundary
options.body: Land the linked PR after a maintainer/security reviewer accepts the Docker metadata exposure warning and confirms audit/configure targets stay aligned.

options.title: Require stronger warning first
options.body: Ask the linked PR to call out SecretRef-backed Docker env metadata exposure more explicitly before merge.

options.title: Reject env delivery
options.body: Pause the PR and design a non-env secret delivery path if Docker metadata exposure is unacceptable for SecretRef-backed values.

recommendation.title: Accept with explicit boundary
recommendation.body: Land the linked PR after a maintainer/security reviewer accepts the Docker metadata exposure warning and confirms audit/configure targets stay aligned.
